ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَا أُقْسِمُ بِيَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ (١)).
There are two views on (لَا). First: it is redundant (zāʾida), just as it was added in the words of the Exalted (لِئَلَّا يَعْلَمَ).
Second: it is not redundant, and there are two views on the meaning:
First: it negates swearing by it, just as swearing by the soul is negated.
Second: «لَا» is a rejection of an implied statement, because they said: "You are fabricating against Allah in your saying 'We will resurrect'"; so He said "No", then began anew and said: "I swear". This is frequent in poetry, for the conjunctive wāw often comes at the beginnings of odes, and a statement is implied there to which it is conjoined. It has also been read «لَأُقْسِمُ». On this there are two views: First: it is the lām of emphasis (tawkīd) entering the imperfect verb, as in the words of the Exalted (وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَيَحْكُمُ بَيْنَهُمْ), and it is not the lām of the oath.
Second: it is the lām of the oath, and the nūn [of emphasis] does not accompany it, relying on the meaning; and because the report of Allah is true, so it may come without emphasis.
It is also said that the verbal clause was likened to the nominal clause, as in the words of the Exalted (لَعَمْرُكَ إِنَّهُمْ لَفِي سَكْرَتِهِمْ. . .).

ukberi-tibyan:4-6.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (بَلَى قَادِرِينَ عَلَى أَنْ نُسَوِّيَ بَنَانَهُ (٤) بَلْ يُرِيدُ الْإِنْسَانُ لِيَفْجُرَ أَمَامَهُ (٥) يَسْأَلُ أَيَّانَ يَوْمُ الْقِيَامَةِ (٦)).
The words of the Exalted (قَادِرِينَ): i.e. «بَلَى نَجْمَعُهَا» (yes, We shall gather them); so «قَادِرِينَ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent.
(أَمَامَهُ) is an adverb (ẓarf), i.e. so that he may disbelieve in what lies ahead. (يَسْأَلُ) is an explanation of «لِيَفْجُرَ».

ukberi-tibyan:12-12.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِلَى رَبِّكَ يَوْمَئِذٍ الْمُسْتَقَرُّ (١٢)).
The words of the Exalted (إِلَى رَبِّكَ): it is the khabar (predicate) of «الْمُسْتَقَرُّ». «يَوْمَئِذٍ» is accusative by a verb that «الْمُسْتَقَرُّ» indicates; «الْمُسْتَقَرُّ» does not govern it, because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) meaning «الِاسْتِقْرَار» (settling) [and a maṣdar does not govern what precedes it]. The meaning is: to Him is the return.

ukberi-tibyan:14-14.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (بَلِ الْإِنْسَانُ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ بَصِيرَةٌ (١٤)).
The words of the Exalted (بَلِ الْإِنْسَانُ): it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), «بَصِيرَةٌ» is its khabar (predicate), and «عَلَى» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the khabar.
There are two views on the feminine ending. First: it is added for intensiveness, i.e. he is a keen witness against himself.
Second: it is according to the sense, i.e. he is a seeing proof against himself; seeing is attributed to the proof for the reason mentioned in [Sūrat] Banī Isrāʾīl.
It is also said that «بَصِيرَةٌ» here is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and the implied form is «ذُو بَصِيرَةٍ» (possessed of insight); but that is valid only by way of clarification (tabyīn).

ukberi-tibyan:22-23.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ نَاضِرَةٌ (٢٢) إِلَى رَبِّهَا نَاظِرَةٌ (٢٣)).
The words of the Exalted (وُجُوهٌ): it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «نَاضِرَةٌ» is its khabar (predicate); beginning with an indefinite noun is permitted because a useful meaning results. (يَوْمَئِذٍ) is an adverb (ẓarf) for the khabar.
The khabar may also be omitted, i.e. «ثَمَّ وُجُوهٌ» (there are faces), with «نَاضِرَةٌ» as an adjective.
As for «إِلَى», it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the latter «نَاظِرَةٌ».
Some of the extremists of the Muʿtazila said: «إِلَى» here is a noun meaning "favour", i.e. awaiting the favour of their Lord, and what is meant is the owners of the faces.

ukberi-tibyan:26-27.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (كَلَّا إِذَا بَلَغَتِ التَّرَاقِيَ (١٦) وَقِيلَ مَنْ رَاقٍ (١٧)). [Translator's note: the verse numbers in the source read 16 and 17; these are verses 26 and 27.]
The words of the Exalted (إِذَا بَلَغَتِ): what governs «إِذَا» is the meaning of (إِلَى رَبِّكَ يَوْمَئِذٍ الْمَسَاقُ), i.e. when it reaches the throat it is raised to Allah the Exalted.
(التَّرَاقِيَ) is the plural of «تَرْقُوَة» (collarbone), which is on the pattern «فَعْلُوَة», not «تَفْعُلَة», since there is no «تَرَقٍّ» in the language.
(مَنْ) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «رَاقٍ» is its khabar (predicate), i.e. who will treat it with incantation to heal it?
It is also said: who will raise it up to Allah, Mighty and Majestic — the angels of mercy or the angels of punishment?

ukberi-tibyan:31-33.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَلَا صَدَّقَ وَلَا صَلَّى (٣١) وَلَكِنْ كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّى (٣٢) ثُمَّ ذَهَبَ إِلَى أَهْلِهِ يَتَمَطَّى (٣٣)).
The words of the Exalted (فَلَا صَدَّقَ): «لَا» means «مَا» (not). There are two views on (يَتَمَطَّى):
First: the alif is a substitute for a ṭāʾ, the root form being «يَتَمَطَّطُ», i.e. he stretches himself out in his walk out of arrogance.
Second: it is a substitute for a wāw, and the meaning is: he stretches his «مَطَا», i.e. his back.

ukberi-tibyan:34-34.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَوْلَى لَكَ فَأَوْلَى (٣٤)).
The words of the Exalted (أَوْلَى لَكَ): there are two views on the pattern of «أَوْلَى»:
First: «فَعْلَى», with the alif for attachment to another pattern (ilḥāq), not for the feminine.
Second: it is «أَفْعَل». On both views it is here a proper name; that is why it does not take tanwīn. This is supported by what is reported from Abū Zayd in al-Nawādir: «هِيَ أَوْلَاةُ», with a tāʾ, as a diptote. On this view «أَوْلَى» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «لَكَ» is the khabar (predicate).
The second view: it is an indeclinable verbal noun (ism fiʿl), meaning: evil after evil has come close to you; and «لَكَ» is for clarification (tabyīn).

ukberi-tibyan:36-40.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَيَحْسَبُ الْإِنْسَانُ أَنْ يُتْرَكَ سُدًى (٣٦) أَلَمْ يَكُ نُطْفَةً مِنْ مَنِيٍّ يُمْنَى (٣٧) ثُمَّ كَانَ عَلَقَةً فَخَلَقَ فَسَوَّى (٣٨) فَجَعَلَ مِنْهُ الزَّوْجَيْنِ الذَّكَرَ وَالْأُنْثَى (٣٩) أَلَيْسَ ذَلِكَ بِقَادِرٍ عَلَى أَنْ يُحْيِيَ الْمَوْتَى (٤٠)).
(سُدًى) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and its alif is a substitute for a wāw.
(يُمْنَى) — with the yāʾ — on the view that the pronoun refers to «الْمَنِيّ», so it is in a genitive position. It may also refer to «النُّطْفَة», because its feminine is not real, and «النُّطْفَة» means water; it would then be in an accusative position, as with the reading with the tāʾ (تُمْنَى).
(الذَّكَرَ وَالْأُنْثَى) is a badal (substitute) for «الزَّوْجَيْنِ». (يُحْيِيَ) is pronounced with the two yāʾs kept distinct (iẓhār) and nothing else, because if the yāʾ were assimilated, a meeting of two vowelless letters would follow, both in pronunciation and in underlying form. And Allah knows best.
